description:
Remnant Retribution

v0.3.0 — a late-game colony crisis — for Starsector 0.98a-RC5

You've spent the campaign hunting Remnant Nexuses for their cores and blueprints. The machines noticed.

Remnant Retribution

is a standalone, vanilla-only colony crisis: every Remnant warship you destroy — and above all every

Nexus

— raises the surviving network's threat assessment of your polity, until it marshals a retaliatory strike against your colonies. The more of the network you've torn down, the weaker its reach... right up until you kill the last Nexus and it throws everything left at you in one final convergence.

Download

RemnantRetribution-0.3.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher.

How the grudge builds

Every Remnant hull your fleet destroys, anywhere in the sector, feeds the network's "grudge":

Frigate — 1Destroyer — 2Cruiser — 4Capital — 8Remnant Nexus — 150 (the single biggest contributor)

As the grudge climbs:

The colony crisis bar ticks up after every battle ("Remnant forces destroyed: +N"), plus a monthly trickle while the network plans.Remnant hunter-killer groups begin patrolling your systems.Around the crisis bar's minor-event stage, a reconnaissance-in-force probes one of your colony systems — a few fleets raiding and assessing, no bombardment. The network's warning shot.Then the retaliation.

The retaliation — and how to beat it

When the crisis fires, a large strike force launches from the nearest surviving Nexus and descends on one of your colonies to

saturation-bomb it on arrival

. This is a live event, not an abstract dice roll: the armada flies to your colony, and if you intercept and destroy it in your own system first, nothing is bombed.

Better yet — avert it at the source.

The moment a retaliation becomes impending, it marshals from a specific surviving Nexus, and

that Nexus's location is revealed on your map

. Race there and destroy it

before the fleet launches

and the retaliation is cancelled outright — no strike at all. (If the network is already reduced to dormant systems with no destructible Nexus, there's nothing to pre-empt and the strike comes anyway.)

Defeat the retaliation force and the grudge is halved — but each strike you beat makes the next one stronger. Machines don't forgive.

Fragment the network — or end it for good

The sector generates with roughly 8–15 live Nexus stations. Each one you destroy permanently weakens the network: monthly progress, hunter-killer presence, and strike strength all scale down with the surviving-Nexus fraction, to a configurable floor (default 25%).

Destroy the

last

Nexus and the shattered network converges for one final, oversized strike (default 1.5× the normal cap). Defeat it and the crisis ends

permanently

— the factor retires and no further grudge accrues. Lose it and the fragments fight on at the floor, every later strike another final convergence — defeat any one of them and the war still ends.

Prefer the old cruelty? Turn off

Permanent Neutralization Possible

for the classic eternal grudge.

Spoils of the hunt

Where there is danger, there is opportunity. Every Nexus you bring down is also loot — all three rewards are on by default and individually toggleable:

Gate Control Fragments — each destroyed Nexus drops a fragment of its Domain-era gate control core in the battle salvage. Take one to any dormant Gate and choose Repair the Gate: that single Gate comes online — no Academy questline required, but no free sector-wide network either. The first repair also yields a working Janus Device (needed to actually transit).Domain-era planetkiller — the last Remnant Nexus guards a planetkiller; destroying it adds the weapon to the salvage (once per campaign, skipped if the vanilla questline already produced one).Path handover — while you carry the planetkiller, an intel entry offers surrendering it to the Luddic Path for the permanent vanilla pather agreement: holy peace, cells stand down for good.

Configuration

Everything above is tunable. With

LunaLib

enabled (optional) you get a live in-game settings menu (Shift+F2) — point values, thresholds, fleet strength, the neutralization rules, all of it. Without LunaLib the mod reads the same values from data/config/settings.json and runs fine standalone.

Requirements & compatibility

Starsector 0.98a-RC5LunaLib — optional, for the in-game config menuVanilla-only — no other hard dependenciesSafe to add to an existing saveRemoving it from a save with the crisis active will break that save — standard for crisis mods

Changelog

v0.3.0

The retaliation force now saturation-bombs the target colony on arrival as a live, interceptable event, instead of resolving abstractly on a timer.Impending retaliations marshal from a specific surviving Nexus whose location is revealed — destroy it before launch to avert the strike entirely.

v0.2.0

Network fragmentation & permanent neutralization; reconnaissance-in-force minor event; Nexus location tracing.

Disclaimer: This post and mod were written using Claude's Fable AI model.

Remnant Retribution
v0.3.0 — a late-game colony crisis — for Starsector 0.98a-RC5

You've spent the campaign hunting Remnant Nexuses for their cores and blueprints. The machines noticed.

Remnant Retribution is a standalone, vanilla-only colony crisis: every Remnant warship you destroy — and above all every Nexus — raises the surviving network's threat assessment of your polity, until it marshals a retaliatory strike against your colonies. The more of the network you've torn down, the weaker its reach... right up until you kill the last Nexus and it throws everything left at you in one final convergence.




Download

RemnantRetribution-0.3.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher.


How the grudge builds

Every Remnant hull your fleet destroys, anywhere in the sector, feeds the network's "grudge":

  • Frigate — 1
  • Destroyer — 2
  • Cruiser — 4
  • Capital — 8
  • Remnant Nexus — 150 (the single biggest contributor)

As the grudge climbs:
  • The colony crisis bar ticks up after every battle ("Remnant forces destroyed: +N"), plus a monthly trickle while the network plans.
  • Remnant hunter-killer groups begin patrolling your systems.
  • Around the crisis bar's minor-event stage, a reconnaissance-in-force probes one of your colony systems — a few fleets raiding and assessing, no bombardment. The network's warning shot.
  • Then the retaliation.


The retaliation — and how to beat it

When the crisis fires, a large strike force launches from the nearest surviving Nexus and descends on one of your colonies to saturation-bomb it on arrival. This is a live event, not an abstract dice roll: the armada flies to your colony, and if you intercept and destroy it in your own system first, nothing is bombed.

Better yet — avert it at the source. The moment a retaliation becomes impending, it marshals from a specific surviving Nexus, and that Nexus's location is revealed on your map. Race there and destroy it before the fleet launches and the retaliation is cancelled outright — no strike at all. (If the network is already reduced to dormant systems with no destructible Nexus, there's nothing to pre-empt and the strike comes anyway.)

Defeat the retaliation force and the grudge is halved — but each strike you beat makes the next one stronger. Machines don't forgive.


Fragment the network — or end it for good

The sector generates with roughly 8–15 live Nexus stations. Each one you destroy permanently weakens the network: monthly progress, hunter-killer presence, and strike strength all scale down with the surviving-Nexus fraction, to a configurable floor (default 25%).

Destroy the last Nexus and the shattered network converges for one final, oversized strike (default 1.5× the normal cap). Defeat it and the crisis ends permanently — the factor retires and no further grudge accrues. Lose it and the fragments fight on at the floor, every later strike another final convergence — defeat any one of them and the war still ends.

Prefer the old cruelty? Turn off Permanent Neutralization Possible for the classic eternal grudge.


Spoils of the hunt

Where there is danger, there is opportunity. Every Nexus you bring down is also loot — all three rewards are on by default and individually toggleable:

  • Gate Control Fragments — each destroyed Nexus drops a fragment of its Domain-era gate control core in the battle salvage. Take one to any dormant Gate and choose Repair the Gate: that single Gate comes online — no Academy questline required, but no free sector-wide network either. The first repair also yields a working Janus Device (needed to actually transit).
  • Domain-era planetkiller — the last Remnant Nexus guards a planetkiller; destroying it adds the weapon to the salvage (once per campaign, skipped if the vanilla questline already produced one).
  • Path handover — while you carry the planetkiller, an intel entry offers surrendering it to the Luddic Path for the permanent vanilla pather agreement: holy peace, cells stand down for good.


Configuration

Everything above is tunable. With LunaLib enabled (optional) you get a live in-game settings menu (Shift+F2) — point values, thresholds, fleet strength, the neutralization rules, all of it. Without LunaLib the mod reads the same values from data/config/settings.json and runs fine standalone.


Requirements & compatibility

  • Starsector 0.98a-RC5
  • LunaLib — optional, for the in-game config menu
  • Vanilla-only — no other hard dependencies
  • Safe to add to an existing save
  • Removing it from a save with the crisis active will break that save — standard for crisis mods


Changelog

v0.3.0
  • The retaliation force now saturation-bombs the target colony on arrival as a live, interceptable event, instead of resolving abstractly on a timer.
  • Impending retaliations marshal from a specific surviving Nexus whose location is revealed — destroy it before launch to avert the strike entirely.

v0.2.0
  • Network fragmentation & permanent neutralization; reconnaissance-in-force minor event; Nexus location tracing.

Disclaimer: This post and mod were written using Claude's Fable AI model.
